scenes.title: THE SUN STARTED FIRES
vo: In eighteen fifty-nine, the Sun set telegraph machines on fire.
Could it happen to our power grid?

scenes.title: LEVEL 1
vo: The Sun can hurl billions of tons of magnetized, charged gas at us, arriving in about three days.

scenes.title: LEVEL 2
vo: Earth's magnetic field is our umbrella.
A storm whose field points south shakes it harder.

scenes.title: LEVEL 3
vo: A shaking magnetic field pushes current through long wires, the same trick a generator uses.
In eighteen fifty-nine, it shocked operators and set telegraphs on fire.

scenes.title: LEVEL 4
vo: In nineteen eighty-nine, a smaller storm overloaded transformers.
Quebec's grid failed in ninety seconds, leaving six million people in the dark.

scenes.title: THE ANSWER
vo: In twenty twelve, a storm that strong missed us by about a week.

scenes.title: IF IT HITS
vo: A direct hit today could cost two trillion dollars and black out up to forty million Americans for weeks,
since giant transformers can take years to repair.

scenes.title: SAVE POINT
vo: So satellites now watch the Sun.
